title: I used Claude to help port my 13 KB JavaScript game to the Dreamcast
author: Slackluster
selftext:
I made SP13KTRA for js13k this year, an anti-gravity racer in 13 KB of JavaScript. Afterwards I wanted to see if AI could handle a real retro port, so I let Claude (in Claude Code) port it to the Dreamcast.

It's now a bootable Dreamcast disc: all 8 tracks, 60 fps, VMU saves, full soundtrack. \[video\]

**Why it worked well for AI**

The game is small, self contained and fully procedural, so there were no assets to convert, just code to translate. And the original served as the answer key: the JS version dumps its tracks, geometry and a scripted drive, and the C++ tests check the port against that. That gave Claude a way to verify its own work instead of guessing.

**How it went**

Claude wrote the C++ port on KallistiOS, working through milestones with a plan and tests for each, plus a PC build of the port for fast iteration. It also wrote a custom renderer for the Dreamcast's PowerVR chip, which took it from 11 fps on first boot to a solid 60 in the Flycast emulator.

My part was mostly playing it, spotting what looked wrong and steering. A few of the tougher bugs needed a human eye to pin down, but Claude did the bulk of the code.

**Try it**

Disc image (only tested in an emulator so far, hardware reports welcome): [https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/SP13KTRA/releases/latest](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/SP13KTRA/releases/latest)

Original in your browser: [https://killedbyapixel.github.io/SP13KTRA/](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/SP13KTRA/)
